title: Part 11
html:
Back through Central India: Amjhora, Mandu, Devghar (the healing of the leper), Vidyanagara and Ramananda Raya, Sambalpur, Rasalkunda (the Marwari brahmana and his son). The return to Puri (pp. 203–222)

[p. 203]

2221There was a great festival in the brahmana's house;
next morning the Lord sets out.

2222The excellent brahmana, coming up lovingly,
pleaded with him long, with folded hands.

2223Taking leave of the brahmana,
my Gora Raya set out in the morning.

2224The vaishya, who had been waiting in hiding,
followed the Lord along the road.

2225Clasping his feet, the vaishya began to weep,
and merciful Chaitanya raised him up.

2226The Lord said, "Holy man, what are you doing, brother?"
The vaishya said, "Have mercy on me, Gosai.

2227I will not let you go — I have recognised you;
give me the dust of your feet and be merciful to me."

2228Smiling, Lord Chaitanya
poured the nectar of the Name of Hari into his ears once.

2229By the Lord's mercy his sins were destroyed,
and the vaishya, greatly blessed, went away.

2230By the Lord's grace the vaishya gave up worldly things,
went far away and lives there, having made a tulasi grove.

2231He does not converse with anyone
and always meditates on Krishna with the flute at his lips.

[p. 204]

2232With his lips he says, "O Hari, have mercy on me;
in your kindness take away all this sinner's suffering."

2233He lives as a hermit and does not go home,
and saying "Hari" he begs alms from door to door.

2234Having shown mercy to the vaishya, Lord Vishvambhara
left the town and went on through the jungle.

2235We all go on through dense jungle,
and for two days we see no town or village.

2236After two days, leaving the jungle,
we reach the town of Amjhora.

2237We writhe in the pangs of hunger,
while my Lord, unperturbed, says "Hari, Hari".

2238The Lord said, "Hari provides food for all."
That same day food came to us of itself.

2239I brought two handfuls of flour I had begged,
and the Lord himself made sixteen rotis.

2240Just then a woman with a child
said, "Give me something — I am dying of hunger.

2241I have no food, no clothing, nothing to eat;
I go along the roads with my child, living on alms."

2242Hearing her words, the merciful Lord
gave her his own share.

[p. 205]

2243The wretched woman went away content,
and the Lord passed the day without food.

2244At night I brought some fruit I had begged,
and the Lord, partaking of the fruit, passed the night.

2245There is a tank of Lakshmana here;
hearing of it in the morning, we go there to bathe.

2246The tank at the edge of the town is most charming,
surrounded by hills, of small extent.

2247When Janaki's throat was parched with thirst,
Lakshmana dug this tank by shooting an arrow.

2248It became famous as the tank of Lakshmana;
Janaki called this tank a great tirtha.

2249A most delightful tank, very deep;
bathing in it, our bodies were cooled.

2250Having bathed in this tirtha, merciful Gora
raises the cry of "Hari" — hearing it, the fear of Yama goes.

2251Next day we go up onto the Vindhya mountains,
where the town of Mandura1 stands in splendour.

2252In the midst of the mountains, inside a cave,
an ascetic lives and performs austerities.

2253Hearing of the ascetic, my Gora Raya
goes there to see him.

[p. 206]

2254The sannyasi thakura is sitting in meditation;
the ascetic's form is most lovely.

2255His body is the colour of molten gold,
and rays of radiance stream out all around.

2256His long, long nails have curled over,
and his white beard covers his chest.

2257Only skin and bone remain, his body emaciated;
his ribs can be seen.

2258He sits motionless, naked;
seeing that form, devotion arose in me.

2259He looks like a wooden image;
opening my eyes wide, I look at his face again and again.

2260Mahaprabhu went and stood before him,
and the ascetic, breaking his meditation, began to look.

2261The moment their eyes met,
the excellent ascetic smiled.

2262Having conversed with the ascetic,
the Lord comes down to the foot of the mountain, to the town of Mandul.

2263On the left the Vindhya range stands in splendour, on the right the Narmada;
from there we reach Devghar in three days.

2264There was a leper in Devghar;
this sick man was named Adi Narayana.

[p. 207]

2265Adi Narayana is the foremost of merchants;
he has much wealth, but his mind is always troubled.

2266Outside the village there is a banyan tree;
the merciful Lord went and sat beside it.

2267The Lord's beauty lights up everything around,
and gradually word spread in the town.

2268Two or four people come to see the sannyasi,
and I go into the town to beg.

2269Ramananda goes to bring flowers,
Govinda Charana went to the riverbank.

2270That day I received unboiled rice as alms,
and Ramananda brings flowers of every kind.

2271Having bathed, my Lord began the worship,
and Govinda Charana brought dry wood.

2272After making the offering, Gora Raya began the Name,
and as he chanted the Name his thrills increased.

2273His body choked with love, he began to dance
and at last fell senseless to the ground.

2274Hearing of this, many people come there,
and that leper came and stood close by.

2275Adi Narayana weeps with folded hands,
and, saying "Save me", wept a great deal.

[p. 208]

2276Adi Narayana is a supreme Vaishnava;
they gave him prasada to eat.

2277Partaking of the prasada with devotion,
he was at once rid of his leprosy.

2278Receiving prasada, his leprosy left him;
hearing this news, many sick people come.

2279Seeing the difficulty, the Lord began to look around,
then, looking at me, made a sign.

2280I took the sandals and set out,
and on that pretext the Lord leaves the town.

2281Then Adi Narayana follows along.
The Lord said, "By Krishna's mercy you are freed —

2282why then do you come with me?
Go home and always meditate on Krishna's feet."

2283Adi Narayana said, "I will not go home;
I will wander from land to land with you."

2284The Lord said, "Go home and enjoy your wealth."
Narayana said, "What use have I for wealth?

2285If you will not take me with you, merciful one,
I shall build a hut and pass my time there."

2286The Lord said, "Go and make a tulasi grove,
and sitting there, pass your time."

[p. 209]

2287Hearing the Lord's words, Adi Narayana gave up everything
and says "Hari, Hari" with his lips.

2288Adi Narayana became the best of holy men;
he passes his time chanting Krishna's name.

2289Bowing at his feet, Adi Narayana
took his leave of the Lord.

2290Thirty kroshas away is the town of Shivana;
in two days Vishvambhara hurries there.

2291East of Shivana is the Mahal mountain;
there the Lord goes, full of love for Krishna.

2292Having seen the Mahal mountain,
the Lord comes to the town of Chandapur.

2293Having had darshan of the goddess Chandi in Chandapur,
Gora goes on to Raipur, remembering Hari.

2294Many people in Raipur, wishing to see him,
came into Chaitanya's presence.

2295Seeing the wretched state of living beings, my Gora Raya
joyfully distributes the Name of Hari from house to house.

2296Then the Lord came to Vidyanagara,
and Ramananda meets him with folded hands.

2297Ramananda Raya came and bowed down,
and the Lord, raising him by the hand, embraced him.

[p. 210]

2298The supreme Vaishnava Raya, drawing far back,
began to weep with great humility.

2299The Lord said, "Raya, come with me;
let us go together and behold Lord Jagannatha.

2300You, I and the Bhatta, going to Nilachala,
will chant the Name of Hari to our hearts' content.

2301With you I shall find great joy in discussing the truth;
come, you shall go with me to Nilachala."

2302Raya said, "You go on ahead;
in a few days I shall go to Nilachala."

2303Hearing this, Mahaprabhu smiled a little,
and, rising in the morning, went north.

2304That day we covered a great distance,
and in six days the four of us reach Ratnapur.

2305Leaving Ratnapur we come to the Mahanadi,
and all go east along its bank.

2306A little further on Mahaprabhu came to Svarnagarh
and gazed attentively at the beauty of the town.

2307Wondrous is the beauty of the fort — what more can I say?
Looking all around, I was astonished.

2308A king named Shantishvara lives in this fort;
a messenger went and told this to the king.

[p. 211]

2309Hearing of us, the worthy king
comes humbly to see the Lord.

2310The most righteous king, seeing the Lord,
with folded hands lay prostrate on the ground.

2311The king said, "Listen, worthy sannyasi,
sanctify my house today.

2312Today, in your kindness, take alms in my house."
Saying this, the king sang many praises.

2313Hearing this, the Lord looked at me,
and I asked the king for alms.

2314The maharaja brought and gave full alms,
and having given the alms, remained standing with folded hands.

2315In the afternoon the maharaja took his leave,
and Mahaprabhu passed the night beneath a tree.

2316In the morning we all go to Sambalpur
and arrive there at dusk.

2317The town, surrounded by hills, is very beautiful;
the Lord passes the night joyfully in Sambalpur.

2318Ten kroshas away is the town of Bhramara;2
there Mahaprabhu hastened on.

2319Many Vaishnavas live in the town of Bhramara;
here the Lord stayed four days.

[p. 212]

2320An Oriya brahmana named Vishnu Rudra
lives here and serves Krishna.

2321The brahmana Vishnu Rudra is very devoted;
the Lord went to see him.

2322Having conversed with Vishnu Rudra,
the Lord goes joyfully on to the town of Pratapnagari.

2323Having given the Name of Hari to the people of this town,
he went on to the town of Dasapalla.

2324Unbelievers, Mayavadis and sufferers, wherever they were,
the Lord made drunk by giving the Name of Hari.

2325Gora is always drunk with joy;
how many sinners he delivered by giving the Name of Hari!

2326Next day we go to Rasalkunda3
and there we see the deity Kurma.

2327Seeing Kurmadeva, the Lord was drunk with love;
tears streamed from both his eyes.

2328With folded hands he sings many hymns to Kurmadeva
and falls crashing to the ground.

2329The people of Rasalkunda are very lacking in devotion;
seeing this, the Lord stays there three days.

2330Calling everyone, men and women alike,
the Lord delivers them by giving the Name of Hari.

[p. 213]

2331By the Lord's mercy everyone grew excited
and began to chant the Name of Hari with devotion.

2332There was a Marwari brahmana here;
his son met the Lord.

2333The brahmana's son said, "Have mercy on me;
give me the dust of your feet, Lord, and take away my sorrow.

2334I am a great unbeliever and know nothing;
give me devotion and save me yourself.

2335My father cannot bear the name of Krishna;
in your mercy give devotion to his heart.

2336This is my great sorrow, that my father hates Krishna;
give devotion to his mind, merciful Lord.

2337When my father sees a Vaishnava he abuses him;
in your mercy remove all his sins.

2338I have heard that you are an abode of mercy;
give me this alms, O merciful one."

2339Hearing this, the Lord put his hand on the boy's back,
and at once devotion arose in his heart.

2340Hearing of this, the brahmana, blind with rage,
ran up to the Lord with a stick in his hand.

2341The brahmana said, "Listen, you hypocrite, you villain!
You have ruined my only son!

[p. 214]

2342I will strike you with this stick;
I will see right now who will protect you!"

2343With folded hands, weeping, the brahmana's son said,
"Merciful one, forgive my father's offence.

2344My father is utterly ignorant and does not recognise you;
count me as a servant of your feet and forgive me."

2345Hearing this, two or four people,
rebuking the Marwari, went for him.

2346The Marwari brahmana heeded no one's words
and, stick in hand, rose up to beat Chaitanya.

2347The brahmana said, "Having made my son a Vaishnava,
you will lead him away with you, beguiling him!

2348Where will you go, having beguiled the boy?
This time I will punish you and teach you a lesson.

2349I have seen many sannyasis with my own eyes;
this time you will get a lesson from me."

2350Smiling, Chaitanya said, "Listen, my brother:
if you want to beat me, you must say the Name of Hari.

2351As many times as you utter the Name of Hari,
so many blows of the stick you may give.

2352If in your anger you want to beat me,
then say the name 'Hare Krishna' with your lips.

[p. 215]

2353Look, here I have bared my back to you;
say 'Hari' once and strike me."

2354Hearing this again, the brahmana's son,
with folded hands, spoke again before the Lord:

2355The boy said, "Lord, forgive my father,
save him from hell.

2356This alms I beg at your lotus feet,
that people may not say, 'Cruel Nimai'."

2357Then the Lord, with a slight smile, said to him,
"In the family into which you have been born

2358no one has any fear of hell;
millions of generations will have a place in Vaikuntha."

2359Saying this, he looked at the brahmana:
"Say, brahmana, say 'Hari' and strike me.

2360Your hard heart is like a desert;
may it become full of sap today by Krishna's mercy.

2361Strike me — that does no harm, brahmana;
just once say 'Hare Krishna' with your lips, brother."

2362Hearing such words, the brahmana began to tremble
and in his fear let his head sink onto his chest.

2363Shrinking with fear, the brahmana cannot see;
weeping in distress, he fell to the ground.

[p. 216]

2364Overwhelmed by the Lord's power, the brahmana
clasped both his feet tightly with both hands.

2365The brahmana said, "Merciful one, I beseech you:
save me from hell.

2366Having committed a great offence, I am afraid;
in your mercy forgive my offence, merciful one.

2367Without understanding, I said so many things to you;
punish or protect me, as you judge best."

2368Seeing the brahmana's humility, Gora, the delight of hearts,
poured the nectar of the Name of Hari into his ears.

2369The brahmana was fulfilled, his mind became pure,
and at last he took his leave, clasping the Lord's feet.

2370Having delivered the unbelieving brahmana, the Lord
went on to the bank of the river Rishikulya.

2371Many rishis live on both banks of the river;
all together they welcomed Gora.

2372When the Lord came to the river Rishikulya,
this news gradually reached Puri.

2373Staying three nights at the abode of Rishikulya,
the Lord sanctified Rishikulya with the Name of Hari.

2374When the Lord came near Alalanatha,
Gadadhara and Murari came running to him.

[p. 217]

2375Khanjan Acharya4 comes with deep love;
lame as he is, he comes ahead of everyone.

2376Sarvabhauma comes, beating two kettle-drums,
and Narahari appears carrying a banner.

2377Haridasa, Ramadasa and Krishnadasa
come eagerly, breathing hard.

2378Jagannatha Dasa and Devaki-nandana,
Junior Haridasa and the singer Lakshmana,

2379Vishnudasa, Puridasa and Damodara,
Narayana Tirtha and Giridhara Dasa —

2380giris, puris, sarasvatis,5 countless brahmanas —
all come to see Gora.

2381A great master at playing the shinga horn,
Balarama Dasa comes, full of thrills.

2382Hundreds of learned gosais appeared,
and my heart began to dance with joy.

2383Some dance, some laugh, some sing songs;
with one mouth that joy cannot be told.

2384Thousands upon thousands, surrounding the Lord,
began the Name, drunk with joy.

2385The Lord went to embrace Murari and Mukunda,
and Gupta6 collapsed near his knees.

[p. 218]

2386Siddha Krishnadasa came and bowed down,
and the Lord, raising him by the hand, embraced him.

2387Gathering together, all the other devotees too
come to take the Lord with them.

2388All the bands of Vaishnavas play their madals;
in his joy the Lord's eyes grow moist.

2389All the Vaishnavas together sing kirtana,
and Gora, the delight of hearts, dances, swaying his head.

2390Seeing Khanjan, the Lord, crying "Hari bol",
spread his arms and embraced him.

2391Gora began to dance with arms outstretched,
and Sarvabhauma fell prostrate at his feet.

2392With folded hands Sarvabhauma began to say,
"The arrow of separation from you has pierced my heart.

2393I am a great fool; that is why I have borne separation from you
and kept my life in me all these days.

2394In your mercy trample my body with your feet;
then I shall know, Lord, that you love me."

2395Saying this, Sarvabhauma rolls on the ground,
and Gora Raya, raising him, embraces him.

2396Thus, raising the cry of "Hari",
they all set off to Puri, taking the Lord.

[p. 219]

2397Hundreds of white, blue and many-coloured banners,
how many kettle-drums sound, rumbling!

2398Some dance, some sing, drunk with joy;
how many people stand pressing close, gazing fixedly!

2399Swaying, Shachi's darling goes along,
while sweet mridangas play, delightful to hear.

2400Raising his arms, Gadadhara began to dance;
Raghunatha Dasa dances, and Damodara too.

2401The Lord asks after Raghunatha affectionately:
"I am very happy to see you."

2402Gora Raya goes to embrace Raghunatha,
but Raghunatha falls and lies prostrate at his feet.

2403On the third day of Magha my Gora Raya7
with all his companions reaches Puri.

2404In the afternoon Mahaprabhu reached Puri,
and millions of people thronged there.

2405With the dust of the road on his feet, the Lord, with many people,
entered the temple and beheld Jagannatha.

2406As he gazed fixedly at Mahavishnu,
tears of love began to stream down.

2407All at once losing consciousness, Gora Raya
immediately fell crashing to the ground.

[p. 220]

2408His matted locks came loose, his kaupina slipped,
his body grey with dust, like the poorest of the poor.

2409All around, the devotees raise the cry of "Hari",
and Sarvabhauma lifted him up and held him.

2410His hair bristled like a kadamba,
and sweat flowed in streams.

2411Regaining consciousness, the Lord stood up
and began to gaze fixedly at Mahavishnu.

2412Sarvabhauma says, "Lord, seeing your own form,
you have made the well of your feeling overflow.

2413Seeing your own image, to teach the people,
you began to weep, drunk with great emotion.

2414Before you is the immovable Vishnu, and you are the moving one;8
why then do you weep, Lord, and play so many tricks?

2415You are Krishna in person, the son of the king of Vraja;
why do you blind my eyes with your moods?

2416Put on airs before someone who does not understand,
but do not hide your own form from me.

2417You are the lifter of Govardhana, the lord of Vrindavana,
the life of the gopis, the refuge of the helpless.

2418You were born in the Yadu race, yet they did not recognise you;
the unfortunate Yadavas understood nothing.

[p. 221]

2419Having got you in my hands, I will not let you go;
take up the flute and show me your own form.

2420A golden doll is painted on your breast,
by whose radiance your dark form cannot be seen."9

2421The Lord said, "Sarvabhauma, talk of something else.
Why do you talk such idle nonsense?

2422Why do you get excited for nothing and say all sorts of things?
Hearing your words, I put my hands over my ears.

2423Calling me the son of the king of Vraja,
why do you make me an offender without cause?

2424Talk of Krishna in your mouth is like nectar;
speak of Krishna, Bhatta, let my soul be soothed."

2425The Bhatta said, "What you, Lord, make me say —
what else can I say, a beast in human form?"

2426The Lord said, "There is no need for more words;
let us all go together today to our place."10

2427Having seen the arati, to the house of Kashi Mishra
he came with all his companions.

2428Just then Sarvabhauma, bringing prasada,
arrived at that place.

2429Gora, the delight of hearts, distributes the prasada,
and all rejoice on receiving the prasada.

[p. 222]

2430In Kashi Mishra's house there is a huge courtyard;
many people come to see the Lord.

2431Staying in Mishra's house, merciful Gora
sings Krishna's glories every day in supreme joy.

2432How can I tell how many people come and go?
Every day there are new joys in Mishra's house.

2433Hearing from people of the Lord's arrival,
how many people of Gauda come to see him!

2434The worthy Bhatta brings prasada every day,
and receiving the prasada, the Lord is filled with joy.

2435Gora, the delight of hearts, joyfully taking the prasada,
distributes the prasada into everyone's hands.

2436Before the prasada there is nama-sankirtana,
and all eat the prasada with loving attachment.

2437"Today we have become blessed" — saying this,
all dance joyfully, clapping their hands.

2438Ramananda, Vasanta and Govinda Charana
took their leave and went to Gauda.

2439Again, to see Gauranga,
hundreds of people come, full of love.

2440Srivasa, Keshava Dasa and Siddha Haridasa
all together come to Chaitanya.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Mandura (Mandua) is Mandu (Mandavgarh), the fortress-city on the spurs of the Vindhyas above the Narmada; below it is called Mandul.
  2. Bhramara is Bamra (Orissa).
  3. Rasalkunda is Russellkonda (Bhanjanagar) in southern Orissa; nearby is Kurmakshetra (Srikurmam).
  4. Khanjan ("the lame") Acharya is apparently Khanja Bhagavan Acharya, one of Chaitanya's companions at Puri.
  5. Giri, puri and sarasvati are names of branches of the order of sannyasis (Dashanami).
  6. Murari Gupta.
  7. That is, a little more than two years after leaving Puri (the departure was on 7 Vaishakha). The traditional chronology (the Charitamrita) allows about two years for the southern pilgrimage.
  8. A play on words: Jagannatha is the achala (immovable) Vishnu, Chaitanya the chala (moving) one.
  9. Another formula of the doctrine of Chaitanya as Krishna concealed by the "golden doll", Radha.
  10. That is, to the place where they will stay (Kashi Mishra's house).
